note: Data backup job types are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 DR metrics, since backups decide the RPO and RTO.

stem: Which of the following types of patches are most typically applied to a hardware device?
explanation: Firmware is a type of software permanently written to the memory built into a hardware device. A firmware update overrides the read-only nature of this memory to update the software. Driver updates, feature updates, and vulnerability patches are typically applied to software products, such as applications and operating systems.
whyWrong: Driver updates are applied to the operating system that talks to the hardware, not to the device itself.
Feature changes are typically delivered as software updates or upgrades.
Vulnerability patches are typically applied to operating systems and applications.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 42

stem: Which of the following software releases is a fix designed to address one specific issue?
explanation: A patch is a relatively small update that is designed to address a specific issue, often a security exploit or vulnerability. Patches do not add features or new capabilities; they are fixes that target a specific area of the software. Updates and upgrades are larger packages that might include new features and/or many different fixes. Drivers are the software products that enable an operating system to communicate with hardware devices.
whyWrong: An update is a larger package that can contain many fixes and new features.
An upgrade is a new version of the software with new features.
A driver lets the operating system communicate with a hardware device.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 43

stem: Unlike individual users, who usually have their operating system patches downloaded and installed automatically, corporate IT departments typically evaluate new patches before deploying them. Which of the following is not a common step in this evaluation process?
explanation: Rolling back, the process of uninstalling a patch to revert to the previous version of the software, is not part of the patch evaluation process. The evaluation process for new patches in a corporate environment usually consists of a research stage, in which you examine the need and purpose for the patch; a testing stage, in which you install the patch on a lab machine; and a backup of the production systems to which you will apply the patch.
whyWrong: Testing the patch on a lab system is a normal evaluation step.
Researching the need and purpose of the patch is a normal evaluation step.
Backing up the production systems before the patch is a normal evaluation step.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 44

stem: Which of the following terms refers to the process of uninstalling a recently released patch to resume using the previous version?
explanation: Rollback is a term used in change management to describe the process of reversing a change that has been made, to restore the original configuration. In the case of patch management, a rollback is the process of uninstalling a recently installed software update. The terms backslide, downgrade, and reset are not used for this procedure. End-of-life is a phase marking the end of a device's marketing, sales, and upgrades. However, the manufacturer might still offer security patches for the product. End-of support (EOS) marks the point at which the manufacturer discontinues all support for the product.
whyWrong: Backslide is not a term used for removing a patch.
Downgrade is not the term this book uses for uninstalling a recent patch.
Reset is not the term used for uninstalling a recent patch.
End-of-life is the life-cycle phase when a product's sales and upgrades end.
End-of-support is the point when the manufacturer stops all support for a product.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 45

stem: A new shipment of bare metal workstations has just arrived, and Alice is responsible for preparing them for deployment on the company network. She first installs the Windows operating system on one computer to build a test configuration. Then, she installs some specialized drivers for the hardware in the computers and the Microsoft 365 productivity applications. After configuring the software and performing an extensive round of testing, Alice is satisfied with the performance of the workstation. She plans to install the operating system, drivers, and office software on all of the workstations, but there are other software products that she will have to install later for users in specific departments. Which of the following are appropriate terms for this basic installation? (Choose two.)
explanation: The golden or baseline configuration is one that administrators will apply to all workstations. In Alice's case, this is not a production configuration because there are other software products to be added later. A sandbox configuration is used for testing purposes only.
whyWrong: A production configuration is the complete configuration in live use, and more software will still be added here.
A sandbox configuration is used for testing only.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 46

stem: An IT department receives a shipment of 20 new computers, and Alice has been assigned the task of preparing them for deployment to end users. The first thing she does is affix a metal tag with a bar code on it to each computer. Which of the following terms BEST describes the function of this procedure?
explanation: Bar coding the new computers enables the IT department to record their locations, status, and conditions throughout their life cycle, a process known as asset tracking. Bar codes are not used for tamper detection and device hardening. Port security refers to switches, not computers.
whyWrong: Bar code asset tags record what the company owns and do not detect tampering.
Device hardening is reducing a device's attack surface, such as by disabling unused services.
Port security is a switch feature that limits which MAC addresses can use a port.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 47

stem: Ralph's company has purchased new computers to replace some of the older workstations currently in use. Ralph has been assigned the task of preparing the old computers for disposal. They will be sold to a local secondhand dealer. In order for the dealer to accept the computers, they must have a functional operating system. Company policy also dictates that the computers be permanently wiped of all applications and data before disposal. Which of the following tasks will Ralph have to perform before the computers are sold? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Deleting files on a hard disk drive leaves them available for retrieval, even though they appear to be gone. A disk wipe utility deletes all of the files on the hard drive and then overwrites the entire disk with zeroes, rendering all files unretrievable. Ralph can then reinstall the operating system to prepare the computer for sale. Performing these two steps eliminates the need to uninstall applications, delete data files manually, or perform a factory reset.
whyWrong: Uninstalling applications is not needed because the disk wipe removes everything.
Deleting files leaves the data recoverable, and the disk wipe removes everything anyway.
A factory reset is not needed because Ralph wipes the disk and reinstalls the operating system.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 48

stem: After starting work as the network administrator of Wingtip Toys, you discover that all of the switches in the company's datacenter have support for remote management, with built-in Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) agents in each port. Which of the following tasks must you perform to be able to gather information from the agents on those switches and display it on a central console? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Install the network management software on a network computer.
Install a management information base (MIB) on each of the switches.
Install an agent on the console computer.
Install an MIB on the console computer.
explanation: An SNMP-based network management system consists of three components: a management console software product installed on a network computer, agents installed on the devices you want to manage, and MIBs for each of the agents. Because the switches support SNMP management and already have agents, they have MIBs also. Therefore, all you have to do is purchase the network management software and install the console on a network computer.
whyWrong: Devices that have built-in SNMP agents already include their MIBs.
The console runs the management software, so it does not need an agent.
The MIBs come with the agents on the managed devices, so none is installed on the console.
The question asks what must be installed or bought, and the existing agents already support management.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 49

stem: Which of the following technologies provides both real-time monitoring of security events and automated analysis of the event information gathered?
explanation: Security information and event management (SIEM) is a product that combines two technologies: security event management (SEM) and security information management (SIM). Together, the two provide a combined solution for gathering and analyzing information about a network's security events. Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is a technology that gathers information about managed devices.
whyWrong: SNMP collects management data from network devices but does not analyze security events.
SEM is only the real-time event monitoring half of SIEM.
SIM is only the information storage and analysis half of SIEM.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 50

stem: Which versions of the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) use unencrypted community strings as their security protection? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: SNMP version 1 (SNMPv1), SNMP version 2 (SNMPv2), and SNMP version 2c (SNMPv2c) all rely on unencrypted community strings that are sent with GET requests as a security mechanism. SNMP version 3 (SNMPv3), the one most often seen today, uses fully encrypted transmissions for more advanced security and does not use a community string.
whyWrong: SNMPv3 uses authentication and encryption instead of plain-text community strings.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 51

stem: Which of the following statements about the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) are not true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: To effectively monitor a network using SNMP, you must be sure that all of the equipment you purchase when designing and building your network supports the protocol.
SNMP is not only the name of a protocol; it is also the name of a network management product.
SNMPv1 and the original SNMPv2 rely on a community string as their only means of security.
Most of the network management products on the market today support SNMPv3.
SNMPv3 is capable of scanning network segments to monitor the availability of their IP addresses.
explanation: SNMP is not the name of a network management product; it is just the name of the protocol that provides a framework for the interaction of the various components in a network management product. SNMPv1 uses a community string, but the original SNMPv2 did not, as it had a newer security system that was not widely adopted. The interim version SNMPv2c retains the community string from version 1 in place of the new version 2 security system. When you see a network interface adapter, switch, router, access point, or other device that purports to be managed or that claims to have network management capabilities, this usually means that the device includes an SNMP agent. Most of today's network management products do support SNMPv3. In addition, many network management products that implement SNMPv3 also include support for the earlier, unprotected versions, such as SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c. SNMPv3 does not perform IP address availability monitoring.
whyWrong: This statement is true, because only devices with SNMP agents can be monitored with SNMP.
This statement is true, because most current management products support SNMPv3.
SNMPv3 does not scan subnets for IP address availability.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 52
note: The book's answer marks only two options, but its explanation also says that SNMPv3 does not perform IP address availability monitoring, so the last statement is also not true and could be a third answer.

stem: Which type of network monitoring utility, such as Wireshark, shows a list of captured packets in one pane and the parsed contents of the selected packet in other panes?
explanation: A packet capture and protocol analyzer application, such as Wireshark, lists the captured packets in its top pane and displays the parsed contents of the selected packet in the bottom panes. System monitors, performance monitors, and log viewers do not display the parsed contents of individual packets.
whyWrong: A system monitor shows system resource use, not the decoded contents of captured packets.
A performance monitor tracks performance counters, not the decoded contents of captured packets.
A log viewer displays log entries, not the decoded contents of captured packets.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 53

stem: Which of the following was created to provide logging services for the Unix sendmail program?
explanation: Syslog is a standard that was designed to facilitate the transmission of log entries generated by a device or process, such as the sendmail Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server, across an Internet Protocol (IP) network to a message collector, called a syslog server. Since its inception, syslog has come to support message logging on other platforms, including operating systems, printers, and routers. Netstat is a program that displays status information about a system's network connections; it does not provide logging services. SNMP is a protocol that carries network management information from agents to a central console; it was not created specifically for sendmail. The Cache Array Routing Protocol (CARP) enables proxy servers to exchange information; it does not provide logging services.
whyWrong: Netstat displays the status of a system's network connections and does not provide logging.
SNMP carries management data from agents to a console and was not created for sendmail.
CARP is a protocol that lets proxy servers share cache information, not a logging service.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 54

stem: You are the administrator of your company's network. Your company wants to perform a baseline analysis of network-related traffic and statistics. They want to track broadcasts, cyclical redundancy check (CRC) errors, and collisions for all traffic traversing a switched network. In addition, they want to generate alerts and cell phone notifications when anomalies occur and provide historical and daily reports for management. They also want to keep track of software distribution and metering. What type of network software product BEST meets these needs?
explanation: The best solution is to implement Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP). This includes a management console, agents, and management information bases (MIBs). SNMP allows you to generate alerts, track statistical network information (historical and current), and produce reports for baseline analysis and troubleshooting. Some SNMP products also allow you to track software distribution and metering. Protocol analyzers are best used for troubleshooting problems in real time and are not used for software distribution and metering. A performance monitor is a tool that allows you to track performance statistics for one system at a time and does not include software distribution and metering. There is no such product as a network traffic monitor.
whyWrong: A protocol analyzer captures and decodes traffic for real-time troubleshooting but does not do software distribution or metering.
A performance monitor tracks statistics for one system at a time and does not do software distribution or metering.
Network traffic monitor is not a product category in this context.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 55

stem: SIEM products combine the capabilities of which of the following? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Security information and event management (SIEM) is a product type that combines two technologies: security event management (SEM) and security information management (SIM). Together, the two provide a combined solution for gathering and analyzing information about a network's security events. Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is a technology that gathers information about managed devices. Syslog is a standard designed to facilitate the transmission of log entries generated by a device or process, such as the sendmail Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server, across an Internet Protocol (IP) network to a message collector, called a syslog server. Neither SNMP nor syslog capabilities is typically included in SIEM products.
whyWrong: Syslog is a standard for sending log messages to a collector, not one of the two technologies that make up SIEM.
SNMP gathers information from managed devices and is not one of the two technologies that make up SIEM.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 56

stem: Which of the following statements about web server logs is not true?
options: To analyze web server activity, you typically use an application that interprets the web server log files.
Web server logs are typically maintained as text files.
Web server logs record the IP addresses of all visiting users.
To interpret web server logs, you use a protocol analyzer.
explanation: A protocol analyzer provides information about network traffic; it does not interpret web server logs. Most web servers maintain logs that track the Internet Protocol (IP) addresses and other information about all hits and visits. The logs are stored as text files and contain a great deal of information, but in their raw form, they are difficult to interpret. Therefore, it is common practice to use a traffic analysis application that reads the log files and displays their contents in a more user-friendly form, such as tables and graphs.
whyWrong: This statement is true, because analysis applications are used to interpret web server logs.
This statement is true, because web server logs are usually plain text files.
This statement is true, because web server logs record the IP addresses of visitors.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 57

stem: Which of the following statements BEST describes a performance baseline?
options: A baseline is an estimation of expected performance levels, based on manufacturers' specifications.
A baseline is a record of performance levels captured under actual workload conditions.
A baseline is a record of performance levels captured under simulated workload conditions.
A baseline is a record of performance levels captured before the system is actually in use.
explanation: A baseline is a record of a system's performance under real-world operating conditions, captured for later comparison as conditions change. The workload during a baseline capture should be genuine, not simulated or estimated. Later measurements are compared with the baseline to find changes and anomalies.
whyWrong: A baseline is measured on the real system, not estimated from manufacturer specifications.
A baseline must reflect the real workload, not a simulated one.
A baseline is captured while the system does its real work, not before it is in use.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 58

stem: Which of the following indicators is typically not included in an operating system's performance monitoring tool, such as the Windows Performance Monitor or the MacOS Activity Monitor?
explanation: Performance monitoring utilities typically provide statistics on the central processing unit (CPU), memory, network, and disk usage, but not computer temperature monitoring. Hardware temperature is normally read from firmware or vendor utilities, not from these operating system tools.
whyWrong: CPU activity is a standard counter in performance monitoring tools.
Memory consumption is a standard counter in performance monitoring tools.
Network utilization is a standard counter in performance monitoring tools.
Storage statistics are a standard counter in performance monitoring tools.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 60

stem: Which of the following syslog message severity levels indicates that a system is unusable?
explanation: Every syslog message includes a single-digit severity code. Code 0 is the most severe, indicating an emergency that has rendered the system unusable. Severity code 1 is an alert message, indicating that immediate action is needed. Severity code 2 is a critical condition message, and code 3 is an error condition. Code 4 is a warning message.
whyWrong: Severity 1 is Alert, which means immediate action is needed.
Severity 2 is Critical, which means a critical condition.
Severity 3 is Error, which means an error condition.
Severity 4 is Warning, which means a warning condition.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 61

stem: Which of the following syslog message severity levels indicates a call for immediate action?
explanation: Every syslog message includes a single-digit severity code. Severity code 1 is an alert message, indicating that immediate action is needed. Code 0 is the most severe, indicating an emergency that has rendered the system unusable. Severity code 2 is a critical condition message, and code 3 is an error condition. Code 4 is a warning message.
whyWrong: Severity 0 is Emergency, which means the system is unusable.
Severity 2 is Critical, which means a critical condition.
Severity 3 is Error, which means an error condition.
Severity 4 is Warning, which means a warning condition.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 62

stem: Which of the following syslog message severity levels indicates that the message is purely informational?
explanation: Every syslog message includes a single-digit severity code. Code 6 indicates that the message is purely informational. Code 0 is the most severe, indicating an emergency that has rendered the system unusable. Severity code 2 is a critical condition message, and code 4 is a warning message. Code 7 is used strictly for debugging.
whyWrong: Severity 0 is Emergency, which means the system is unusable.
Severity 2 is Critical, which means a critical condition.
Severity 4 is Warning, which means a warning condition.
Severity 7 is Debug, which is used only for debugging messages.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 63

stem: A Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) console can inform administrators when a managed device requires attention. For this to occur, the agent in the device first has to send a message to the console. What is the term used for a message sent by an SNMP agent to the central console?
explanation: Messages that SNMP agents send to consoles when an event needing attention occurs are called traps. Alerts and notifications are terms for the messages that the console sends to administrators. A ping is an Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) echo request message sent from one TCP/IP computer to another. A flow describes the transaction between network devices, but it is not an SNMP feature.
whyWrong: An alert is a message that the console sends to administrators, not a message from the agent.
A notification is a message that the console sends to administrators, not a message from the agent.
A ping is an ICMP echo request, not an SNMP message.
A flow is a record of traffic between devices, not an SNMP message.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 64

stem: Which of the following metrics would you typically not find displayed by an interface monitor?
explanation: The term rollback refers to the process of uninstalling or downgrading an update patch; it has nothing to do with monitoring a network interface. An interface monitor does typically display the number of transmission errors that occur on an interface, the amount of the available bandwidth that the interface is using, and the number of packets that have been dropped due to errors or discards.
whyWrong: Error rate is a standard metric that an interface monitor displays.
Bandwidth utilization is a standard metric that an interface monitor displays.
Packet drops are a standard metric that an interface monitor displays.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 65

stem: Which of the following is not a statistic that you would typically find in a server performance baseline?
explanation: Performance baselines characterize hardware performance, so the OS update history would be of little or no use for future comparisons. A baseline typically consists of CPU, memory, disk, and network performance statistics.
whyWrong: CPU utilization is a standard baseline statistic.
Disk transfer rate is a standard baseline statistic.
Network transmission speed is a standard baseline statistic.
Memory utilization is a standard baseline statistic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 67

stem: Log management typically consists of which of the following tasks? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Logs frequently contain sensitive information, so securing them with the appropriate permissions is an essential part of log management. Logs also can grow to overwhelm the storage medium on which they are stored, so cycling is a technique for managing log size by configuring it to delete the oldest record each time a new one is added. Rollback and utilization are not log management tasks.
whyWrong: Rollback is reversing a patch or change, not a log management task.
Utilization is a performance metric, not a log management task.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 68

stem: Which of the following security information and event management (SIEM) processes performs searches for specific criteria, during specific time frames, in logs located on different computers?
explanation: In SIEM, forensic analysis is a process of searching logs on multiple computers for specific information based on set criteria and time periods. Data aggregation is a process of consolidating log information from multiple sources. Correlation is the process of linking logged events with common attributes together. Retention is the long-term storage of log data.
whyWrong: Data aggregation consolidates log data from many sources into one place.
Correlation links logged events that share common attributes.
Retention is the long-term storage of log data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 69

stem: Which of the following terms BEST describes the security information and event management (SIEM) process of consolidating log information from multiple sources?
explanation: In SIEM, data aggregation is a process of consolidating log information from multiple sources. Forensic analysis is a process of searching logs on multiple computers for specific information based on set criteria and time periods. Correlation is the process of linking logged events with common attributes together. Retention is the long-term storage of log data.
whyWrong: Forensic analysis searches logs on many systems for set criteria in set time periods.
Correlation links logged events that share common attributes.
Retention is the long-term storage of log data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 70

stem: Which of the following Windows applications would you MOST LIKELY use to create a baseline of system or network performance?
explanation: Performance Monitor is a Windows application that can create logs of specific system and network performance statistics over extended periods. Such a log created on a new computer can function as a baseline for future troubleshooting. Event Viewer is a Windows application for displaying system log files; it cannot create a performance baseline. Syslog is a log compilation program originally created for Unix systems; it does not create performance baselines. Network Monitor is a protocol analyzer. Although it can capture a traffic sample that can function as a reference for future troubleshooting efforts, this capability cannot be called a performance baseline.
whyWrong: Event Viewer displays the Windows event logs and cannot create a performance baseline.
Syslog is a logging standard from Unix and does not create performance baselines.
Network Monitor is a protocol analyzer that captures packets, not a performance baseline tool.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 71

stem: Which of the following is the database used by the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) to store information gathered from agents distributed about the network?
explanation: A management information base (MIB) is the database on an SNMP console where all of the information gathered from the network is stored. A trap is an alert message that SNMP agents send to the network management console. Syslog is a standard for message logging components. Security information and event management (SIEM) is a combination tool that uses information gathered from logs and network devices to provide a real-time analysis of the network's security condition.
whyWrong: A trap is an alert message that an agent sends to the console.
Syslog is a standard for sending log messages to a collector.
SIEM is a security product that collects and analyzes logs and events.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 72

stem: Which of the following are not SNMP components?
explanation: Cyclical redundancy checks (CRCs) are faults that occur when data does not arrive at its destination in the same state as when it was sent; they are not Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) components. Management information bases (MIBs), traps, and object identifiers (OIDs) are all components of a Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) implementation. API integration, such as that using the Representational State Transfer (REST) architecture, can enable clients on the network to access SNMP information through simple web-based requests, rather than giving them direct access to the SNMP back end.
whyWrong: MIBs are the databases of managed objects in an SNMP system.
Traps are the event messages that SNMP agents send to the console.
OIDs identify each managed object in an SNMP MIB.
API integration, such as REST, can give clients web-based access to SNMP data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 73

stem: Which of the following abbreviations describes a product that combines real-time monitoring of security events and automated analysis of the event information gathered?
explanation: Security information and event management (SIEM) is a product that combines two technologies: security event management (SEM) and security information management (SIM). Together, the two provide a combined solution for gathering and analyzing information about a network's security events. Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is a technology that gathers information about managed devices. SEIM and SEM/SIM are not correct abbreviations for security information and event management.
whyWrong: SNMP collects management data from network devices but does not analyze security events.
SEIM is not the correct abbreviation for security information and event management.
SEM/SIM names the two parts of SIEM, not the abbreviation for the combined product.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 75

stem: Which of the following troubleshooting tools enables you to capture all of the packets transmitted in network traffic to a buffer, analyze the protocols used in the packets, and display the output?
explanation: A protocol analyzer captures all network traffic, interprets the protocol headers and fields, and displays the output. The Event Viewer displays system, application, and security event logs on a single computer. Performance monitor tracks the values of specific metrics, but it does not capture packets. A management console is a remote monitoring and management device that queries Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) agents.
whyWrong: Event Viewer shows the event logs of one computer and does not capture packets.
A performance monitor tracks metric values and does not capture packets.
A management console queries SNMP agents and does not capture packets.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 76

stem: Which of the following switch features enables administrators to capture traffic generated by the computers connected to the switch?
explanation: Port mirroring is a feature found in some switches that takes the form of a special port that runs in promiscuous mode. This means that the switch copies all incoming traffic to that port, as well as to the dedicated destination ports. By connecting a protocol analyzer to this port, an administrator can access all of the network's traffic. Stateful packet inspection is a firewall feature that enables the device to examine Network and Transport layer header fields, looking for patterns that indicate damaging behaviors, such as IP spoofing, SYN floods, and teardrop attacks. Trunking is a switch feature that enables administrators to create VLANs that span multiple switches. Service-dependent filtering is a firewall feature that blocks traffic based on Transport layer port numbers.
whyWrong: Stateful packet inspection is a firewall feature that tracks connections and looks for attack patterns.
Trunking carries traffic for many VLANs over one link between switches.
Service-dependent filtering is a firewall feature that blocks traffic by port number.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 77

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the function of an administrative network monitoring tool that can perform an ad hoc network discovery?
options: The administrator starts the tool, and it scans the local subnet, displaying a list of the MAC addresses associated with it.
The administrator specifies an IP address, and the tool scans all of the well-known port numbers at that address for active services.
The administrator enters a range of IP addresses, and the tool attempts to perform a traceroute test for each one.
The administrator enters a range of IP addresses, and the tool scans each address to determine if a device is using it.
The administrator creates a network discovery schedule and identifies the network address of the subnet to be scanned.
explanation: An ad hoc network discovery is a one-time scan of a range of IP addresses to determine whether they are in use. The tool does not scan the port numbers for each address, list the MAC addresses, or perform traceroute tests. While scheduled network discoveries are possible, the term ad hoc refers to a one-time, on-demand procedure.
whyWrong: An ad hoc discovery scans IP addresses for active devices, not a list of MAC addresses.
Scanning one address for open ports is a port scan, not a network discovery.
An ad hoc discovery does not run a traceroute to each address.
A scheduled discovery runs on a set schedule, while ad hoc means a one-time, on-demand scan.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 78

stem: Which of the following is the primary aim of an organization's security incident response policies?
options: To know how to respond to a particular incident
To prevent an incident from occurring again
To identify the cause of an incident
To document the procedures leading up to an incident
explanation: While incident response policies might include the process of responding to an incident and identifying and documenting its cause, the primary function of incident response policies is to ensure that the same incident does not happen again. Responding to the incident, finding its cause, and documenting it all serve that goal of preventing a repeat.
whyWrong: Knowing how to respond is part of the policy, but the main aim is to keep the incident from happening again.
Finding the cause is part of the process, but the main aim is to keep the incident from happening again.
Documenting the events is part of the process, but the main aim is to keep the incident from happening again.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 79
note: Incident response is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 DR testing, the closest topic.

stem: Which of the following tasks are not considered to be part of an IT department's incident response plan? (Choose two.)
options: Performing tabletop exercises to prepare for an incident
Containing the damage caused by an incident
Remediating the damage caused by an incident
Rebuilding an infrastructure destroyed by an incident
explanation: Tabletop exercises and validation tests can be a useful part of an incident preparedness plan, but they are not part of the incident response. Once a network infrastructure has been partially or completely destroyed, rebuilding it is no longer a matter of incident response; the responsibility passes over to the disaster recovery plan, which requires a different set of policies. Stopping, containing, and remediating an incident are all considered incident response policies.
whyWrong: Stopping an ongoing incident is a core part of incident response.
Containing the damage is a core part of incident response.
Remediating the damage is a core part of incident response.
Validation tests are part of incident preparedness.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 80
note: Incident response is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 DR testing, the closest topic. The book's answer marks two options, but its explanation also says that validation tests are not part of the incident response, so that option could be a third answer.

stem: Which of the following are occurrences that are typically addressed by an IT department's incident response policies? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Attacks, hardware failures, and crashes are all events that can be addressed by incident response policies that define what is to be done to analyze and remediate the problem. An electrical fire typically would not be addressed by an IT department's incident response team; it is a job for trained firefighters. Once the fire is out, the company's response falls under the heading of disaster recovery.
whyWrong: An electrical fire is handled by firefighters, and recovery afterward falls under disaster recovery.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 81
note: Incident response is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 DR testing, the closest topic.

stem: Which of the following Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) levels provides fault tolerance by storing parity information on the disks, in addition to the data?
explanation: RAID is a technology for storing data on multiple hard disk drives, providing fault tolerance, increased performance, or both. The various RAID levels provide different levels of functionality and have different hardware requirements. RAID 5 combines disk striping with distributed storage of parity information, which provides fault tolerance. The parity information enables the array to rebuild a disk whose data has been lost. RAID 0 uses data striping only (blocks written to each disk in turn), which does not provide any form of fault tolerance. RAID 1 provides fault tolerance through disk mirroring. RAID 10 creates fault-tolerant mirrored stripe sets.
whyWrong: RAID 0 stripes data across disks with no redundancy, so it gives no fault tolerance.
RAID 1 provides fault tolerance by mirroring, not by storing parity.
RAID 10 provides fault tolerance with mirrored stripe sets, not parity.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 82
note: RAID is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 high-availability approaches as a fault tolerance method.

stem: Which of the following RAID levels uses disk striping with distributed parity?
explanation: Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) is a technology for storing data on multiple hard disk drives, providing fault tolerance, increased performance, or both. The various RAID levels provide different levels of functionality and have different hardware requirements. RAID 5 combines disk striping (blocks written to each disk in turn) with distributed storage of parity information, for fault tolerance. RAID 0 provides data striping only. RAID 1 provides disk mirroring. RAID 10 creates mirrored stripe sets.
whyWrong: RAID 0 is striping only, with no parity.
RAID 1 is disk mirroring, with no parity.
RAID 10 is mirrored stripe sets, with no parity.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 84
note: RAID is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 high-availability approaches as a fault tolerance method.

stem: Which of the following is not a fault tolerance mechanism?
explanation: Mean time between failure (MTBF) is a hardware specification used to predict the approximate lifetime of a component; it does not refer to any type of fault tolerance mechanism. Port aggregation, clustering, and uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs) are all mechanisms that provide fault tolerance in the event of network adapter, server, and power failures, respectively.
whyWrong: Port aggregation provides fault tolerance if a network adapter or link fails.
Clustering provides fault tolerance if a server fails.
A UPS provides fault tolerance if the power fails.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 85
note: MTBF is a 3.3 DR metric; the question tests which items are fault tolerance mechanisms, so it is tagged with 3.3 high-availability approaches.

stem: Which of the following is not a type of server load balancing mechanism?
explanation: Load balancing is a method of distributing incoming traffic among multiple servers. Network address translation (NAT) is a routing mechanism that enables computers on a private network to share one or more public Internet Protocol (IP) addresses; it is not a load balancing method. Domain Name System (DNS) round-robin, multilayer switching, and content switching are all mechanisms that enable a server cluster to share client traffic.
whyWrong: Round-robin DNS spreads client requests across servers by rotating the addresses it returns.
Content switching sends requests to different servers based on the requested content.
Multilayer switching can distribute client traffic among the servers in a cluster.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 86

stem: Which of the following is an element of high availability systems that enables them to automatically detect problems and react to them?
explanation: Highly available systems often have redundant failover components that enable them to continue operating even after a failure of a router, switch, hard disk, server, or other component. Backups, snapshots, and cold sites can all contribute to a system's high availability, but they do not function automatically.
whyWrong: Backups support availability but must be restored manually.
Snapshots support availability but do not react to failures automatically.
A cold site must be equipped and brought online manually.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 87

stem: Which of the following RAID levels does not provide fault tolerance?
explanation: Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) is a technology for storing data on multiple hard disk drives, providing fault tolerance, increased performance, or both. The various RAID levels provide different levels of functionality and have different hardware requirements. RAID 0 uses data striping only (blocks written to each disk in turn), which does not provide any form of fault tolerance. RAID 1 provides disk mirroring; RAID 5 combines disk striping with distributed storage of parity information; and RAID 10 creates mirrored stripe sets—these three levels all provide fault tolerance.
whyWrong: RAID 1 provides fault tolerance by mirroring.
RAID 5 provides fault tolerance with distributed parity.
RAID 10 provides fault tolerance with mirrored stripe sets.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 88
note: RAID is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 high-availability approaches as a fault tolerance method.

stem: Which of the following disaster recovery mechanisms can be made operational in the LEAST amount of time?
options: All of the options are the same.
explanation: Cold, warm, and hot backup sites differ in the hardware and software they have installed. A cold site is just a space at a remote location. The hardware and software must be procured and installed before the network can be restored; therefore, it is the least expensive and takes the most time. A warm site has hardware in place that must be installed and configured. A hot site has all of the necessary hardware already installed, configured, and ready to go in the event of a disaster. A warm site is more expensive than a cold site, and a hot site is the most expensive and takes the least amount of time to be made operational.
whyWrong: A cold site is only space, and its hardware must be bought and installed, so it takes the most time.
A warm site has hardware that must still be set up and configured, so it takes longer than a hot site.
The sites differ in how much is ready, so the time to make them operational differs.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 89

stem: Which of the following datacenter disaster recovery mechanisms is the LEAST expensive to implement?
explanation: A cloud site is the least expensive to implement. Cold, warm, and hot backup sites differ in the hardware and software they have installed, but they all require the maintenance of a facility for a new datacenter. A cold site is just a space at a remote location. The hardware and software must be procured and installed before the network can be restored. It is the least expensive of the cold, warm, and hot options and takes the most time. A warm site has hardware in place that must be installed and configured. A hot site has all of the necessary hardware already installed, configured, and ready to go in the event of a disaster. A warm site is more expensive than a cold site, and a hot site is the most expensive and takes the least amount of time to be made operational. A cloud site is a virtual facility maintained with a cloud service provider. The cloud site does not require physical space or physical hardware, so it is the least expensive.
whyWrong: A cold site is the cheapest of the physical sites, but it still needs a facility to be maintained.
A warm site needs a facility and installed hardware, so it costs more than a cold site.
A hot site is the most expensive, because everything is installed and ready.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 90

stem: Which of the following terms defines how long it will take to restore a server from backups if a complete system failure occurs?
explanation: The recovery time objective (RTO) specifies the amount of time needed to restore a server from the most recent backup if it should fail. This time interval depends on the amount of data involved and the speed of the backup medium. A recovery point objective (RPO) specifies how much data is likely to be lost if a restore from backups should be necessary. This figure is based on the frequency of the backups and the amount of new data generated by the system. Business contingency planning (BCP) is an umbrella term for procedures enacted to keep the organization functioning in the event of a disaster. A management information base (MIB) is a database used by Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) systems.
whyWrong: RPO is how much data can be lost, measured as the time since the last backup.
BCP is the overall planning to keep the business running during a disaster.
A MIB is the database of managed objects in SNMP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 91

stem: In a disaster recovery scenario, which of the following terms applies to devices that are not repairable?
explanation: Mean time to failure (MTTF) refers to devices that will eventually fail once and then be discarded, rather than repaired. Mean time between failure (MTBF), mean time to repair (MTTR), and mean down time (MDT) all refer to devices that will eventually fail and then be repaired and reused.
whyWrong: MTBF is the expected time a repairable component runs between failures.
MTTR is the average time needed to repair a failed component.
MDT is the mean down time of a device that is repaired and reused.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 92
note: MTTF and MDT are not named in the N10-009 objectives; the question tests the DR metrics, so it is tagged with 3.3 DR metrics.

stem: A network load balancing cluster is made up of multiple computers that function as a single entity. Which of the following terms is used to describe an individual computer in a load balancing cluster?
explanation: In a network load balancing cluster, each computer is referred to as a host. Other types of clusters use other terms. For example, in a failover cluster, each computer is called a node. The terms server and box are not used in clustering.
whyWrong: Node is the term for a computer in a failover cluster, not in a load balancing cluster.
Server is not the term used for a member of a load balancing cluster.
Box is not a clustering term.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 94

stem: Which of the following disaster recovery mechanisms is the LEAST expensive to implement?
options: All of the options cost the same.
explanation: Cold, warm, and hot backup sites differ in the hardware and software they have installed. A cold site is just a space at a remote location. The hardware and software must be procured and installed before the network can be restored. It is the least expensive. A warm site has hardware in place that must be installed and configured. A hot site has all of the necessary hardware installed and configured. A warm site is more expensive than a cold site, and a hot site is the most expensive.
whyWrong: A warm site has installed hardware, so it costs more than a cold site.
A hot site is the most expensive, because everything is installed and ready.
The sites differ in how much is ready, so their costs differ.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 96

stem: Which of the following can be provided by clustering servers?
explanation: A cluster is a group of computers configured with the same application that function as a single unit. The cluster can function as a fault tolerance mechanism by failing over from one server to the next, when necessary, or provide load balancing by distributing traffic among the servers.
whyWrong: Clustering does provide fault tolerance, but it also provides load balancing and failover.
Clustering does provide load balancing, but it also provides fault tolerance and failover.
Clustering does provide failover, but it also provides fault tolerance and load balancing.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 97

stem: When you configure NIC teaming on a server with two network adapters in an active-passive configuration, which of the following services is provided?
explanation: NIC teaming enables you to combine the functionality of two network interface cards (NICs) in one connection. However, when you configure a NIC team to use an active-passive configuration, one of the network adapters remains idle and functions as a fault tolerance mechanism. If the other NIC should fail, the passive NIC becomes active. In this configuration, NIC teaming does not provide load balancing, server clustering, or traffic shaping.
whyWrong: In active-passive mode only one adapter carries traffic, so there is no load balancing.
Server clustering joins several servers, not two adapters in one server.
Traffic shaping prioritizes traffic and is not provided by NIC teaming.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 98

stem: Which of the following is not a load balancing mechanism?
explanation: Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) level 1 is a fault tolerance mechanism that is also known as disk mirroring. A storage subsystem writes data to two or more disks at the same time so that if a disk fails, the data remains available. Because data is written to the disks at the same time, this RAID level does not provide load balancing. NIC teaming balances a network traffic load among two or more network interface cards (NICs), whereas server clustering and Domain Name System (DNS) round-robin balance a traffic load among multiple servers.
whyWrong: NIC teaming can balance traffic across two or more adapters.
Server clustering can balance traffic across several servers.
Round-robin DNS balances traffic by rotating the server addresses it returns.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 99

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between cold, warm, and hot backup sites?
options: Whether the backup site is owned, borrowed, or rented
The age of the most recent backup stored at the site
The cost of the hardware used at the site
The time needed to get the site up and running
explanation: Cold, warm, and hot backup sites are disaster recovery mechanisms that enable a network to be activated at a remote location when a catastrophe occurs. The temperature refers to a site’s readiness to assume the role of the network. A cold site is just a space at a remote location. The hardware and software must be procured and installed before the network can be restored. A warm site has hardware in place that must be installed and configured. It takes less time to restore the network than at a cold site, but more than at a hot site. A hot site has all of the necessary hardware installed and configured. The network can go live as soon as the most recent data is restored.
whyWrong: Cold, warm, and hot do not describe who owns the site.
The temperature does not refer to the age of the backups at the site.
Cost differs between the sites, but the terms describe how ready each site is.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 100

stem: Which of the following specifications would you most want to examine when comparing hard disk models for your new Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) array?
explanation: Mean time between failure (MTBF) specifies how long you can expect a device to run before it malfunctions. For a hard disk, this specification indicates the life expectancy of the device. Service-level agreements (SLAs) and acceptable use policies (AUPs) are not specifications associated with hard disk drives. Mean time to repair (MTTR) can conceivably be specified for a hard disk, but hard disk drives in a RAID array are typically replaced, not repaired.
whyWrong: An SLA is a contract with a service provider, not a disk specification.
An AUP is a policy for employees, not a disk specification.
MTTR matters little for disks in an array, because failed disks are replaced, not repaired.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 101

stem: Which of the following RAID levels provides fault tolerance with the smallest amount of usable disk space? (Choose two.)
explanation: Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) is a technology for storing data on multiple hard disk drives, providing fault tolerance, increased performance, or both. The various RAID levels provide different levels of functionality and have different hardware requirements. RAID 1 provides disk mirroring, and RAID 10 creates mirrored stripe sets. Both provide fault tolerance by maintaining two copies of every stored file, for a usable disk space percentage of 50 percent. Some mirroring configurations store more than two copies of each file, for even less usable space. RAID 0 provides data striping only, with no fault tolerance. RAID 5 combines disk striping (blocks written to each disk in turn) with distributed storage of parity information, for fault tolerance with a usable disk space percentage of at least 66 percent.
whyWrong: RAID 0 gives no fault tolerance.
RAID 5 gives at least 66 percent usable space, more than mirroring.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 102
note: RAID is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 high-availability approaches as a fault tolerance method.

stem: Disk mirroring and disk duplexing are both fault tolerance mechanisms for hard disk data storage. Which of the following statements about disk mirroring and disk duplexing is true?
options: Disk mirroring enables a server to survive the failure of a disk drive.
Disk duplexing enables a server to survive the failure of a disk controller.
Disk mirroring enables a server to survive the failure of a disk drive or a disk controller.
Disk duplexing enables a server to survive the failure of a disk drive or a disk controller.
explanation: Disk mirroring and disk duplexing both use multiple hard disk drives to store duplicate copies of all data. However, disk duplexing calls for each disk to be connected to a separate controller so that the data remains available if there is a disk failure or a disk controller failure. Mirroring uses one controller for both disks, so a controller failure takes both copies offline.
whyWrong: This statement is true but incomplete, because mirroring also survives a disk failure but not a controller failure, and duplexing survives both.
Duplexing survives a controller failure, but this statement leaves out that it also survives a disk failure.
Mirroring uses one controller, so it cannot survive a controller failure.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 103
note: RAID is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 high-availability approaches as a fault tolerance method.

stem: You are installing a new Windows server with two hard disk drives in it, and you want to use RAID to create a fault-tolerant storage system. Which of the following RAID levels can you configure the server to use?
explanation: Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) is a technology for storing data on multiple hard disk drives, providing fault tolerance, increased performance, or both. The various RAID levels provide different levels of functionality and have different hardware requirements. RAID 1 provides disk mirroring for fault tolerance and requires two or more disk drives. RAID 0 provides data striping only, with no fault tolerance. RAID 5 combines disk striping (blocks written to each disk in turn) with distributed storage of parity information for fault tolerance, but it requires a minimum of three disk drives. RAID 10 creates mirrored stripe sets and requires at least four disk drives.
whyWrong: RAID 0 stripes data across disks with no redundancy, so it gives no fault tolerance.
RAID 5 needs at least three disks.
RAID 10 needs at least four disks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 104
note: RAID is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 high-availability approaches as a fault tolerance method.

stem: Which of the following RAID levels provide fault tolerance without using parity data? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) is a technology for storing data on multiple hard disk drives, providing fault tolerance, increased performance, or both. The various RAID levels provide different levels of functionality and have different hardware requirements. RAID 1 and RAID 10 both use disk mirroring to provide fault tolerance, which does not require parity data. RAID 0 uses data striping only (blocks written to each disk in turn), which does not provide any form of fault tolerance. RAID 5 combines disk striping with distributed storage of parity information.
whyWrong: RAID 0 stripes data across disks with no redundancy, so it gives no fault tolerance.
RAID 5 uses striping with distributed parity.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 105
note: RAID is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 high-availability approaches as a fault tolerance method.

stem: If you back up your network by performing a full backup every Wednesday at 6:00 p.m. and incremental backups in the evening on the other days of the week, how many jobs would be needed to completely restore a computer with a hard drive that failed on a Monday at noon?
explanation: An incremental backup is a job that backs up all of the files that have changed since the last backup of any kind. Therefore, to restore a system that failed on Monday at noon, you would have to restore the most recent full backup from the previous Wednesday and the incrementals from Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. That is one full backup plus four incrementals, for five jobs.
whyWrong: One job would restore only the full backup, without the later changes.
Two jobs would be enough only with differential backups.
Six jobs would include an incremental that has not run yet.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 106
note: Data backup job types are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 DR metrics, since backups decide the RPO and RTO.

stem: For a complete restore of a computer that failed at noon on Tuesday, how many jobs would be needed if you performed full backups to tape at 6:00 a.m. every Wednesday and Saturday and incremental backups to tape at 6:00 a.m. every other day?
explanation: An incremental backup is a job that backs up all of the files that have changed since the last backup of any kind. Therefore, to restore a system that failed on Tuesday at noon, you would have to restore the most recent full backup from the previous Saturday and the incrementals from Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday morning. That is one full backup plus three incrementals, for four jobs.
whyWrong: One job would restore only the full backup, without the later changes.
Two jobs would be enough only with differential backups.
Three jobs would leave out one of the three incrementals since Saturday.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 107
note: Data backup job types are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 DR metrics, since backups decide the RPO and RTO.

stem: If you back up your network by performing a full backup every Wednesday at 6:00 p.m. and differential backups in the evening on the other six days of the week, how many jobs would be needed to completely restore a computer with a hard drive that failed on a Tuesday at noon?
explanation: A differential backup is a job that backs up all the files that have changed since the last full backup. Therefore, to restore a system that failed on Tuesday at noon, you would have to restore the most recent full backup from the previous Wednesday and the most recent differential from Monday.
whyWrong: One job would restore only the full backup, without the later changes.
Six jobs would be needed only with incremental backups.
Seven jobs is more than one full backup and one differential.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 108
note: Data backup job types are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 DR metrics, since backups decide the RPO and RTO.

stem: Why does performing incremental backups to a hard drive, rather than a tape drive, make it possible to restore a server with a single job, rather than multiple jobs?
options: Because hard drives hold more data than tape drives.
Because hard drives can transfer data faster than tape drives.
Because hard drives are random access devices and tape drives are not.
Because hard drives use a different block size than tape drives.
explanation: Data is stored on tape drives in a linear fashion. Once you write backup data to a tape, you cannot selectively replace individual files. When you perform a restore job, you might have to restore the most recent full backup, followed by incremental backups, which overwrites some of the full backup files with newer ones. Hard disk drives are random access devices, meaning that individual files can be written to and read from any location on the disk. When you perform incremental backup jobs to a hard disk, the software can restore data using any version of each file that is available. Data capacity, transfer speed, and block size are not relevant.
whyWrong: Capacity does not decide how many restore jobs are needed.
Transfer speed does not decide how many restore jobs are needed.
Block size does not decide how many restore jobs are needed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 109
note: Data backup job types are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 DR metrics, since backups decide the RPO and RTO.

stem: Which of the following is not a fault tolerance mechanism?
explanation: Simple Network Monitoring Protocol (SNMP) is a means of tracking the performance and functionality of network components. Software or firmware components called agents are embedded in network devices and communicate with a central monitoring console. SNMP does not provide fault tolerance. An uninterruptible power supply (UPS) is a battery backup device that enables a computer to continue functioning in the event of a power failure. Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) level 1 is a disk mirroring mechanism that provides fault tolerance by maintaining duplicate copies of all stored data. Clustering is a mechanism by which multiple servers function as a single unit, running the same application, so that if a server should fail, the others continue to function.
whyWrong: A UPS provides fault tolerance if the power fails.
RAID 1 provides fault tolerance by mirroring data.
Clustering provides fault tolerance if a server fails.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 110

stem: Which of the following is a term for a read-only copy of a data set made at a specific moment in time?
explanation: A snapshot is a read-only copy of a data set taken at a specific moment in time. By creating a snapshot and then backing it up, you can be sure that no data corruption has occurred due to version skew. A hot site is an alternative network location in which all hardware and software is installed and ready. Incrementals and differentials are types of backup jobs.
whyWrong: An incremental is a backup job that copies files changed since the last backup.
A hot site is a fully equipped alternate location for DR.
A differential is a backup job that copies files changed since the last full backup.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 111
note: Data backup job types are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 3.3 DR metrics, since backups decide the RPO and RTO.

stem: Which of the following statements about backing up a firewall's state and backing up its configuration are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: A backup of a firewall's state contains more data than a backup of its configuration.
A backup of a firewall's configuration contains more data than a backup of its state.
A backup of a firewall's state contains the exact same data as a backup of its configuration.
A backup of a firewall's state includes its configuration.
A backup of a firewall's configuration includes its state.
explanation: A backup of a firewall's state includes its configuration as well as other elements, such as templates and policies. The state therefore contains more data than the configuration. Backing up the state is therefore the more complete way to restore a firewall.
whyWrong: The configuration is only part of the state, so it contains less data.
The state also includes templates and policies, so the two backups are not the same.
The configuration does not include the state, because the state is the larger set.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 112

stem: Redundant servers running in an active-active configuration provide which of the following advantages that the same servers in an active-passive configuration do not? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: In an active-active configuration, servers can balance the incoming client load between them. Because the active servers are all servicing clients, the overall performance of the cluster is increased. Both active-active and active-passive configurations provide fault tolerance. Data encapsulation is not a factor in either configuration.
whyWrong: Both active-active and active-passive setups give fault tolerance, so it is not an extra advantage.
Data encapsulation has nothing to do with how redundant servers are configured.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 113

stem: To build a network with redundant Internet connections that ensures full fault tolerance, it is necessary to use which of the following?
explanation: Access to the Internet can be interrupted by a failure on the Internet service provider's (ISP's) network, by a failure on the wide area network (WAN) provider's network, or by a router failure on the local network. Building redundancy into all of these elements is the best way to ensure continuous access to the Internet.
whyWrong: Different ISPs alone leave the WAN link and the local router as single points of failure.
Different WAN connections alone leave the ISP and the local router as single points of failure.
Different routers alone leave the ISP and the WAN link as single points of failure.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 114
note: Provider and path diversity; mapped to 3.3 High-availability approaches as the closest topic.

stem: Installing redundant firewalls in a parallel configuration, with a router that splits incoming traffic between the two firewalls, provides which of the following benefits? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Configuring the router to split incoming packets between the two firewalls provides load balancing and a resulting performance increase. If one firewall should fail, the parallel arrangement enables the other one to take over the processing of all incoming packets, providing fault tolerance. Two firewalls in parallel do not provide additional security.
whyWrong: Two firewalls in parallel apply the same rules, so they do not add security over one firewall.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 115
note: Stem rewritten to describe the book's figure (a router splitting traffic between two parallel firewalls).

stem: In which of the following DNS transactions does the querying system generate a recursive query? (Choose two.)
options: A DNS client sends the server name `www.adatum.com` from a URL to its designated DNS server for resolution.
A client's DNS server sends a request to a root domain server to find the authoritative server for the `com` top-level domain.
A client's DNS server sends a request to the `com` top-level domain server to find the authoritative server for the `adatum.com` domain.
A client's DNS server, which has been configured to function as a forwarder, sends the server name `www.adatum.com` from a URL to its ISP's DNS server for resolution.
A client's DNS server sends a request to the `adatum.com` domain server to find the IP address associated with the server name `www`.
explanation: When a client sends a name resolution query to its DNS server, it uses a recursive request so that the server will take on the responsibility for resolving the name. The only other use of recursive requests is in the case of a forwarder, which is configured to pass that responsibility on to another server. All of the other queries issued by the client's server to the various domain authorities are iterative queries.
whyWrong: A client's query to its own DNS server is also recursive, but the book's key does not list it.
A query from the client's DNS server to a top-level domain server is iterative.
A query from the client's DNS server to the authoritative domain server is iterative.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 116
note: The book's key lists the root server query and the forwarder query, but its own explanation says the client-to-server query and the forwarder query are recursive; the root server query is iterative, so the key looks wrong (the first and fourth options are correct in practice).

stem: Which of the following devices would you MOST LIKELY configure to function as a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server?
explanation: Most wireless routers are designed to provide connecting workstations with IP addresses and other TCP/IP configuration parameters. Switches and bridges are Data link layer devices, and hubs are Physical layer devices, none of which are capable of providing clients with Network layer IP addresses.
whyWrong: An unmanaged switch has no configuration interface and cannot run a DHCP server.
A hub is a Physical layer device that only repeats signals.
A bridge is a Data link layer device that forwards frames and does not assign addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 117

stem: Which of the following protocols are responsible for assigning IP addresses to hosts? (Choose two.)
explanation: DHCP and BOOTP are both designed to allocate IP addresses to hosts. The primary difference between the two is that DHCP is capable of dynamic allocation and BOOTP is not. DNS resolves hostnames into IP addresses, and ARP resolves IP addresses into Data link layer hardware (or MAC) addresses. FTP is designed to transfer files between systems and has no role in IP address allocation.
whyWrong: ARP resolves IP addresses into MAC addresses.
DNS resolves hostnames into IP addresses.
FTP transfers files between systems.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 118

stem: Which of the following Domain Name System (DNS) resource records is used only for reverse name resolution?
explanation: Like A and AAAA records, pointer records (PTRs) contain hostnames and IP addresses, but they are used for reverse name resolution—that is, resolving IP addresses into hostnames. A mail exchange (MX) record specifies the mail server that the domain should use. Canonical name (CNAME) records specify aliases for a given hostname. An AAAA resource record maps a hostname to an IPv6 address for name resolution purposes.
whyWrong: An MX record names the mail server for a domain.
A CNAME record gives an alias for a hostname.
An AAAA record maps a hostname to an IPv6 address for forward lookups.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 3: Network Operations, Review Questions question 119
