Client-to-site is a type of VPN connection, and bring your own device (BYOD) is a policy defining whether and how users are permitted to connect their personal devices to the network.
whyWrong: Client-to-site is a type of VPN connection.
In-band access goes through the production network, but a console port avoids it.
BYOD is a policy for personal devices on the network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 7: Practice Test 2, Practice Test 2 question 25

stem: Virtual private networks (VPNs) use a data transmission technique called tunneling, which encapsulates a data packet within another packet for transmission over a network connection, typically using the Internet. The system also encrypts the entire encapsulated data packet for protection. Split tunneling is a variation of this method that provides which of the following advantages? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Access to local network devices while connected to the VPN
explanation: A standard VPN typically uses full tunneling, in which all of the system's network traffic is encapsulated and encrypted for transmission. Split tunneling is a variation of this method in which only part of the system's traffic uses the VPN connection; the rest is transmitted over the network in the normal manner. Administrators can select which applications and devices use the VPN. Split tunneling can conserve the Internet bandwidth used by the VPN and provide access to local network services without the need for encapsulation. Split tunneling does not provide additional data integrity protection or improved performance through multiplexing.
whyWrong: Split tunneling does not add data integrity protection.
Split tunneling does not speed up data through multiplexing.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 7: Practice Test 2, Practice Test 2 question 51

stem: Which version of the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) uses as its security mechanism two separate unencrypted community strings?
explanation: SNMP version 1 (SNMPv1), SNMP version 2 (SNMPv2), and SNMP version 2c (SNMPv2c) all rely on unencrypted community strings that are sent with GET requests as a security mechanism. However, SNMPv2c uses two separate community strings, one for read-write and one for read-only access. SNMP version 3 (SNMPv3) uses fully encrypted transmissions for more advanced security and does not use a community string.
whyWrong: SNMPv1 is the original version with basic community string security.
SNMPv2 added protocol features, but its party-based security model was not widely adopted.
SNMPv3 uses encrypted transmissions and user-based security instead of community strings.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 7: Practice Test 2, Practice Test 2 question 75
note: The book credits SNMPv2c with two separate community strings; in practice SNMPv1 also uses separate read-only and read-write strings, so the distinction is the book's.

stem: You are negotiating an agreement with a provider for your company's email service. You have been told to require a 99.99 percent guaranteed rate of service reliability, but the provider is only willing to guarantee 99 percent. Eventually, you and the provider agree on a compromise of 99.9 percent. Which of the following documents will include the negotiated language on this particular point?
explanation: The agreed upon 99.9 percent guaranteed availability will be part of a service-level agreement (SLA), which is a contract between a provider and a subscriber that specifies the percentage of time that the contracted services are available. None of the other three options contain the guaranteed reliability language. Acceptable use policies (AUP) specify whether and how employees can use company-owned hardware and software resources. A nondisclosure agreement (NDA) specifies what company information employees are permitted to discuss outside the company. A bring your own device (BYOD) policy specifies the personal electronics that employees are permitted to use on the company network and documents the procedures for connecting and securing them.
whyWrong: An AUP sets how employees may use company hardware and software.
A BYOD policy covers personal devices on the company network.
An NDA says what company information may be shared outside the company.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 7: Practice Test 2, Practice Test 2 question 79

stem: Ralph is installing a pair of redundant servers and must choose whether to run them in an active-active or active-passive configuration. Running the servers in an active-active configuration provides which of the following advantages that the same servers in an active-passive configuration do not? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: In an active-active configuration, servers can balance the incoming client load between them. Because the active servers are all servicing clients, the overall performance of the cluster is increased. Both active-active and active-passive configurations provide fault tolerance. Data encapsulation is not a factor in either configuration.
whyWrong: Both active-active and active-passive configurations provide fault tolerance, so it is not an advantage of active-active alone.
Data encapsulation is a networking process that neither server configuration changes.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 7: Practice Test 2, Practice Test 2 question 84

stem: In the Domain Name System (DNS), a zone is a contiguous area of the DNS namespace for which authority is delegated to one or more DNS servers. Which of the following DNS resource record types specifies the IP addresses of the authoritative DNS servers for a particular zone?
explanation: The name server (NS) resource record identifies the authoritative servers for a particular DNS zone. Pointer (PTR) resource records are used to resolve IP addresses into hostnames. Mail exchange (MX) records identify the mail servers for a particular domain. Service locator (SRV) records identify the designated servers for a particular application. None of these other options identify the authoritative servers for a zone.
whyWrong: A PTR record maps an IP address to a hostname for reverse lookups.
An SRV record identifies the servers that provide a specific service or application.
An MX record identifies the mail servers for a domain.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 7: Practice Test 2, Practice Test 2 question 87

stem: Your company's office building is having a fire inspection, and you are the only person on duty in the datacenter. The inspector from the fire department is reviewing the company's asset inventory and asks you where they can find documentation about all chemicals and equipment used in the company's datacenter. You lead the inspector to the director's office, but you are not sure what the documents he needs are called. Which of the following document types contains this information?
explanation: Material safety data sheets (MSDSs) are documents created by manufacturers of chemical, electrical, and mechanical products that specify the potential risks and dangers associated with them, particularly in regard to flammability and the possibility of toxic outgassing. A properly documented network should have MSDS documents on file for all of the chemical and hardware products used to build and maintain it. MSDSs can be obtained from manufacturers or the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Electrostatic discharges (ESDs), nondisclosure agreements (NDAs), and bring your own device (BYOD) policies are not concerned with the dangers inherent in building contents.
whyWrong: ESD is electrostatic discharge, a hazard to components rather than a document.
An NDA is an agreement that keeps business information confidential.
A BYOD policy sets the rules for employees who use their own devices at work.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 7: Practice Test 2, Practice Test 2 question 89
note: Safety data sheets are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with the closest topic, documentation.

stem: Which of the following is part of a network’s physical topology?
options: A printer plugged into a nearby desktop computer
A password for the wireless network
File permission settings on a desktop computer
explanation: Physical topology mostly refers to a network’s hardware and how computers, other devices (such as printers), and cables or radio signals work together to form the physical network. Operating systems, passwords, and file permission settings are all part of a network’s logical topology.
whyWrong: An operating system is software and belongs to the logical topology.
A wireless password is a logical setting, not a piece of hardware.
File permissions are logical settings that control access to data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 1: Introduction to Networking, Self-Check question 1

stem: Which network diagram shows a logical topology?
explanation: Network mapping is the process of discovering and identifying the devices on a network. A network map shows logical connections and addressing information. Diagrams of physical layouts include floor plans and rack diagrams. A baseline configuration is a change management concept that defines a stable state to be achieved and maintained before attempting future changes.
whyWrong: A rack diagram shows where devices physically sit in a rack.
A floor plan shows the physical layout of a building and its equipment.
A baseline configuration is a change management concept, not a network diagram.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Self-Check question 4

stem: What documentation will indicate how many copies you can install of a particular application?
explanation: Licensing restrictions might define who is allowed to use an application and for how long, how many users are allowed to install or access it, whether the application can be made available over a company’s network or the Internet, and how many backup copies of the application may be stored. A baseline configuration defines a stable state to be achieved and maintained in a system before attempting future changes. SOPs (standard operating procedures) help ensure consistency as different employees perform the same complex tasks. An SLA (service level agreement) is a legally binding contract or part of a contract that defines, in plain language and in measurable terms, the aspects of a service provided to a customer.
whyWrong: A baseline configuration defines a stable system state to maintain before future changes.
An SOP describes how employees perform a complex task consistently.
An SLA defines the measurable service levels a provider owes its customer.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Self-Check question 5

stem: When an Internet connection goes down, what business document defines a customer’s options for paying a reduced rate?
explanation: An SLA (service-level agreement) specifies options for compensation if outages exceed defined thresholds. An MOU (memorandum of understanding) documents the intentions of two or more parties to enter into a binding agreement. An SOW (statement of work) documents in detail the work that must be completed for a particular project. An RFP (request for proposal) is a request to vendors to submit a proposal for a product or service your company wants to purchase.
whyWrong: An MOU documents the intention of two or more parties to enter into a binding agreement.
An SOW details the work that must be completed for a project.
An RFP asks vendors to submit proposals for a product or service.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Self-Check question 6

stem: Which is longer for a reliable device?
explanation: The MTBF (mean time between failures) is the average amount of time that will pass for devices before the next failure is expected to occur. This should be significantly longer than the MTTR (mean time to repair), which is the average amount of time required to repair a device once it fails. A SPoF (single point of failure) is a single device, connection, service, or any other resource on which other resources depend and which has no backup. SSOT (single source of truth) refers to information gathered into a central repository.
whyWrong: MTTR is the average time needed to repair a device, which should be short for a reliable device.
A SPoF is a resource with no backup that other resources depend on, not a time measurement.
SSOT means a single source of truth, a central repository of information.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Self-Check question 7

stem: Which change is designed to close a security vulnerability without affecting other components of an application?
explanation: A software patch is a correction, improvement, or enhancement to software. It corrects a bug, closes a vulnerability, or adds minor enhancements to only part of the software, leaving most of the code untouched. A software rollback is the process of reverting to a previous version of software after attempting to patch or upgrade it. A software upgrade is a major change to a software package that enhances the functionality and features of the software, while also correcting bugs and vulnerabilities. New software is installed on a device.
whyWrong: A rollback returns software to an earlier version after a patch or upgrade.
An upgrade is a major change that adds features to much of the software.
An installation puts new software on a device rather than fixing existing code.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Self-Check question 8

stem: Which change management principle must you apply to all changes regardless of scope or impact?
options: Apply the change as soon as possible.
explanation: Some change management principles apply to any type of change, including the requirement to document each change throughout the process. More extensive or expensive changes typically must progress through a formal change management process, which might include submitting a change request document and acquiring review board approval. Patches or upgrades should always be thoroughly tested and planned, although updates that close a critical security vulnerability should be prioritized and applied as soon as reasonably possible.
whyWrong: Review board approval is usually required only for larger or more expensive changes.
Only urgent changes, such as fixes for critical vulnerabilities, are applied as soon as possible.
A formal change request is usually required only for more extensive changes.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Self-Check question 9

stem: What information should never be included in the name of a web server?
explanation: A good naming convention describes a device without giving away too much information to potential attackers. Device names often include the building, the floor, the department, or the purpose of the device. A username, especially an administrative one, gives an attacker half of a set of sign-in credentials. It should never appear in a device name.
whyWrong: A building location is a normal field in a top-down naming convention.
The device's purpose on the network helps technicians identify it and is a common naming field.
A department name or acronym is a common and recognizable naming field.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Review Questions question 5
note: Device naming conventions are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with the closest topic, documentation.

stem: Which document should be adjusted if your budget for a project has changed?
explanation: An SOW (statement of work) documents in detail the work that must be completed for a project. It includes the specific tasks, the deliverables, the timeline, and the costs. When the budget for a project changes, the SOW must be updated to match.
whyWrong: An SLA defines the service levels a provider owes a customer, not a project budget.
An RFP asks vendors for proposals before a project is contracted.
An MOU documents the intention to enter into an agreement and does not detail the project work.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Review Questions question 6
note: The SOW is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with the closest topic, documentation.

stem: A network administrator stores passwords in a safe that no one else has access to. This is a(n) _________________.
explanation: Password documentation must be kept very secure, but more than one person should have access to it. If the only person who can open the safe is unavailable, nobody can retrieve the high-security passwords. A resource that others depend on and that has no backup is a single point of failure (SPoF).
whyWrong: Redundancy means having a backup, which is the opposite of one person holding the only access.
A password manager is an application that stores passwords, not a locked safe that only one person can open.
An SOP is a written procedure that helps employees perform a task consistently.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Review Questions question 7
note: SPoF is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with documentation because the chapter discusses it under password documentation.

stem: Configuration monitoring is intended to prevent _________________.
explanation: Small changes are sometimes made to a system without approval or documentation. Over time, this slow movement away from the intended configuration is called configuration drift. Configuration monitoring compares systems to a baseline or golden configuration to find and prevent this drift.
whyWrong: A baseline configuration is the stable state you want to keep, not something to prevent.
A golden configuration is the optimized configuration that other systems are compared to.
Configuration versions are tracked on purpose by version control.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Review Questions question 8

stem: Historic configurations are typically kept for the purpose of _________________.
explanation: An audit reviews historic configuration changes to find out whether they were properly evaluated and approved. It also checks whether the changes gave the desired effect and whether configurations still conform to compliance requirements. Version control keeps each historic configuration so that it can be audited or rolled back.
whyWrong: Automation applies configurations automatically and does not need historic configurations.
Discovery finds the devices on a network rather than reviewing past configurations.
Compliance is checked through audits, which is why the historic records serve auditing.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Review Questions question 9

stem: In what period should you schedule a network change?
explanation: A maintenance window is the period in which a change will be implemented, usually during off-hours. Many organizations keep a regularly scheduled maintenance window for changes. Everyone who might be affected must be informed of the window and agree to it in advance.
whyWrong: A rollback reverts a change that failed, not a period for scheduling changes.
Automatic failover moves service to a backup system when a failure occurs.
Decommissioning removes a device from service and is not a scheduling period.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Review Questions question 10

stem: You’ve been assigned the task of inventorying all IT assets in your department. You’ve been given a stack of purchase receipts, some user manuals, and an old spreadsheet of items scheduled for maintenance. What is the FIRST step you should take to begin developing updated and relevant documentation for ongoing inventory management?
options: List an administrative account’s username and password for each device on the network.
List all components on the network.
explanation: Inventory management is the monitoring and maintaining of all the assets that make up a network. The first step is to list all the components on the network, such as hardware, software, and licenses. Once you know what devices you have, you can track, update, and dispose of them.
whyWrong: Interviewing users can add details later, but it does not start the inventory.
Network requirements are part of planning a network, not the start of an inventory.
Administrative credentials must be stored securely and are not the start of an inventory list.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Scenario-Based Questions question 4

stem: You’re shopping for a new router, and you’ve found three models that will meet your needs and your budget. After some recent problems with another router on your network, which of the following metrics do you want to maximize to avoid similar problems with the new router?
explanation: MTBF (mean time between failures) is the average amount of time that passes before a device's next failure is expected. A higher MTBF means a more reliable device. After problems with an unreliable router, you want the new router's MTBF to be as high as possible.
whyWrong: EOS is the date when a vendor stops supporting a product.
EOL is the date when a vendor stops selling or making a product.
MTTR is the average time to repair a failed device, which you want to keep low.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 2: Infrastructure and Documentation, Scenario-Based Questions question 5

stem: When your computer requests a DNS lookup, which DNS server holds the most reliable information for that DNS record?
explanation: The primary DNS server is the authoritative name server for the organization, which holds the authoritative DNS database for the organization’s zones. The caching DNS server and forwarding DNS server might contain needed DNS information in their cache, but this information could potentially be outdated. Root DNS servers play a role in DNS resolution by holding information used to locate the TLD (top-level domain) servers. These TLD servers hold information about the authoritative servers owned by various organizations.
whyWrong: A caching DNS server might hold the record in its cache, but the cached copy could be outdated.
A forwarding DNS server might also hold a cached copy that could be outdated.
Root DNS servers only locate the TLD servers and do not hold the organization's records.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing, Self-Check question 8

stem: Which DNS record type is listed first in a zone file?
explanation: An SOA (start of authority) record is listed at the beginning of the zone file and gives important information about the zone, such as a contact email address, when the zone was last updated, how long the zone information is valid until it should be refreshed, and necessary information for how to perform a zone transfer. A (address) records, AAAA (address for IPv6) records, and CNAME (canonical name) records are placed later in the zone file and provide mapping information.
whyWrong: A records map host names to IPv4 addresses and come later in the zone file.
AAAA records map host names to IPv6 addresses and come later in the zone file.
CNAME records hold alternative names for a host and come later in the zone file.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing, Self-Check question 9
note: The SOA record is not named in the N10-009 record types; tagged with name resolution.

stem: Which DNS record type is used to find an FQDN from a given IP address?
explanation: A PTR (pointer) record is used for reverse lookups to provide a host name when you know an IP address. A (address) records find IPv4 addresses when the host name is known. CNAME (canonical name) records hold alternative names for a host. An MX (mail exchange) record identifies an email server.
whyWrong: An A record finds an IPv4 address when the host name is known.
A CNAME record holds an alternative name for a host.
An MX record identifies an email server.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing, Self-Check question 10

stem: Which DNS server offers the most current resolution to a DNS query?
explanation: The primary DNS server is the authoritative name server for an organization's zones. It holds the original, current copy of the zone's records. Caching and forwarding servers might answer from their cache, but that information could be outdated.
whyWrong: TLD servers know which authoritative servers hold a domain's records, but they do not hold those records.
Root servers only point to the TLD servers.
A caching server might return a cached answer that is out of date.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing, Review Questions question 6

stem: Which type of DNS record identifies an email server?
explanation: An MX (mail exchange) record identifies the email server for a domain. Mail servers look up the MX record to find where to deliver email. A domain can have several MX records with different priorities.
whyWrong: An AAAA record maps a host name to an IPv6 address.
A CNAME record holds an alternative name for a host.
A PTR record maps an IP address to a host name.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing, Review Questions question 8

stem: You have just brought online a new secondary DNS server and notice your network-monitoring software reports a significant increase in network traffic. Which two hosts on your network are likely to be causing the increased traffic and why?
options: The caching and primary DNS servers, because the caching server is requesting zone transfers from the primary server.
The secondary and primary DNS servers, because the secondary server is requesting zone transfers from the primary server.
The root and primary DNS servers, because the primary server is requesting zone transfers from the root server.
The web server and primary DNS server, because the web server is requesting zone transfers from the primary DNS server.
explanation: A secondary DNS server holds a read-only copy of the zone that it gets from the primary DNS server. To get that copy, it requests a zone transfer from the primary server. When a new secondary server comes online, its first zone transfers and the regular updates that follow can add noticeable traffic between the two servers.
whyWrong: A caching server stores answers from earlier queries and does not request zone transfers.
Root servers do not hold the organization's zone, so the primary server does not request zone transfers from them.
A web server is a DNS client and does not request zone transfers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing, Scenario-Based Questions question 1

stem: You are the network manager for a computer training center that allows students to bring their own laptops to class for learning and taking notes. Students need access to the Internet, so you have configured your network’s DHCP server to issue IP addresses automatically. Which DHCP option should you modify to make sure you are not wasting addresses used by students who have left for the day?
explanation: The lease time sets how long a client may keep an IP address before it must renew it. When students leave, their addresses stay assigned until the leases expire. A short lease time, for example a few hours, returns unused addresses to the pool quickly so new students can get them.
whyWrong: Changing the address pool changes how many addresses exist, but leases still stay assigned to absent laptops.
The DNS server address option tells clients where to resolve names and has no effect on address use.
A reservation always gives one address to one specific device, which suits servers rather than visiting laptops.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 3: Addressing, Scenario-Based Questions question 2

stem: You need to remote into a Linux server in another building on your network. Which of the following protocols should you use?
explanation: The SSH (Secure Shell) suite of protocols is included with all modern UNIX and Linux distributions and with macOS client operating systems. RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) is a Microsoft proprietary protocol used by Windows. SFTP (Secure FTP) is a file-transfer version of SSH that includes encryption and authentication. A VPN (virtual private network) is a network connection encrypted from end to end that creates a private connection to a remote network, not a server in another portion of the same network.
whyWrong: RDP is a Microsoft protocol for remote desktop sessions, mainly used with Windows.
SFTP transfers files over SSH but does not give you a remote session.
A VPN connects you to a remote network rather than to a server on your own network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols, Self-Check question 7

stem: You’re working from home and need to access a file server at the office while working in an application from your work desktop. At the same time, you often stream music in your browser. Which VPN type will be most efficient while still meeting your needs?
explanation: A split tunnel VPN will only capture traffic destined for the corporate network, such as communication with the file server and the work desktop, and the client can use local network resources to stream music from the Internet, which will reduce latency and will use fewer corporate network resources. A full tunnel VPN captures all network traffic, whether destined for the Internet or for the corporate network. A host-to-host VPN creates a VPN tunnel directly between two devices and would not provide access to other resources, such as music streaming. A site-to-site VPN connects multiple sites across a WAN and requires more expensive equipment than a client-to-site VPN for the split tunnel configuration.
whyWrong: A full tunnel VPN sends all traffic, including the music stream, through the corporate network.
A host-to-host VPN connects only two devices and would not reach the other resources you need.
A site-to-site VPN connects whole sites across a WAN and needs more expensive equipment.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols, Self-Check question 8

stem: Which secured tunneling protocol might be able to cross firewalls where IPsec is blocked?
explanation: OpenVPN is an open-source VPN protocol that uses OpenSSL for encryption. Its traffic can cross many firewalls where IPsec might be blocked. It is both highly secure and highly configurable.
whyWrong: IKEv2 is used with IPsec, so it is blocked where IPsec is blocked.
L2TP is usually paired with IPsec for security and is blocked with it.
GRE is a tunneling protocol that does not encrypt traffic by itself.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols, Review Questions question 9
note: OpenVPN is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with client-to-site VPN.

stem: You’re working on a network performance issue after receiving several trouble tickets from users, and you need to check the configuration of a router in a nearby building. Which utility should you use to access the router securely over the network?
explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) gives you an encrypted, authenticated command-line session on a remote device. Network administrators use it to manage routers and switches over the network. Telnet does the same job but sends all data in plain text, so it is not secure.
whyWrong: Telnet gives remote access but sends everything, including passwords, in plain text.
SFTP transfers files securely but does not give you a command session on the router.
RDP is used for remote desktop sessions on Windows computers, not for router configuration.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 4: Protocols, Scenario-Based Questions question 3

stem: Which of these WAN services is backed by an SLA?
explanation: Leased line performance is backed by SLA-enforced uptime, repair time, and possibly backup options. DSL, cable, and fiber broadband all rely on a “best-effort” service level to provide up to the advertised bandwidth, and actual performance varies considerably during busy usage.
whyWrong: DSL is a best-effort service whose performance varies during busy usage.
Fiber broadband is a best-effort service without SLA-enforced uptime.
Cable broadband is a best-effort service whose actual performance varies considerably.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Self-Check question 2

stem: What can protect your company from a lawsuit if data is recovered from a discarded device?
explanation: A CEED (Certificate of Electronic Equipment Destruction) is a certificate provided by a disposal service, and it provides legal protection should data later be recovered from your devices. For all companies that provide credit card services, including accepting, storing, processing, or transmitting credit card data, the PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards) sets requirements for keeping that information secure. The GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) defines broad protections in the EU (European Union) for PII (personally identifiable information) and standards for how to handle breaches affecting protected data. A DLP (data loss prevention) solution identifies sensitive data on the network and prevents it from being copied or transmitted off the network. Disposal services provide it as part of decommissioning old devices.
whyWrong: PCI DSS sets security requirements for companies that handle credit card data.
GDPR defines protections for personal data in the EU.
DLP finds sensitive data and prevents it from being copied or sent off the network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management, Self-Check question 9

stem: A company wants to have its employees sign a document that details some project-related information that should not be discussed outside the project’s team members. What type of document should they use?
explanation: An NDA (nondisclosure agreement) defines what information is confidential and who may see it. Employees who sign it agree not to share that information with others. It is the right document to keep project details within the project team.
whyWrong: An AUP defines how employees may use company systems and networks.
MDM software manages and secures mobile devices.
A BYOD policy sets the rules for employees who use their own devices at work.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control, Scenario-Based Questions question 1
note: The NDA is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with the closest topic, documentation.

stem: You’re about to deploy a new website for a startup company, and you need to register the website’s URL with a new A record. Which protocol will ensure this information is validated so visitors can find your website on the Internet?
explanation: DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) adds digital signatures to DNS records. Resolvers use the signatures to check that a record is valid and has not been changed. This protects visitors from being sent to a spoofed site through forged DNS data.
whyWrong: RADIUS authenticates users who connect to a network.
SAML exchanges authentication data for single sign-on.
TACACS+ authenticates administrators who manage network devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control, Scenario-Based Questions question 3

stem: Which log type would most likely be used FIRST to investigate the cause of high numbers of dropped packets?
explanation: Historical traffic logs can be used to investigate security breaches, confirm regulatory compliance, and investigate network performance issues. A system log tracks information on a single device and will not be helpful until you know which device(s) to check. The data in an audit log is thorough enough to retroactively prove compliance and is often used in forensics investigations; due to the level of detail included, an audit log is not likely the best place to start investigating a network problem. There’s no such thing as a jitter log.
whyWrong: A system log tracks events on one device and does not help until you know which device to check.
There is no such thing as a jitter log.
An audit log is very detailed and is used to prove compliance, so it is not the place to start.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Self-Check question 2

stem: Which of the following would be assigned an OID?
explanation: A device, such as a web server, can be managed by an NMS server, typically using UDP ports 161 and 162. Each managed device may contain several managed objects, which can be any characteristic of the device that is monitored, including components such as a switch’s interface, processor temperature, or memory utilization. Each managed object is assigned an OID (object identifier).
whyWrong: An NMS server is the system that manages the devices, not a managed object.
A web server is a managed device that contains managed objects, not a managed object itself.
A UDP port is how SNMP messages travel, not a managed object.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Self-Check question 3

stem: Which of the following cloud services would display a line chart indicating web server traffic over the previous 30 days?
explanation: Real-time monitoring data and log data, such as historical web server traffic, can be streamed to dashboards for human evaluation. Notifications might be transmitted either by email or text message, also called SMS, or they can automatically prompt support ticket generation; notifications typically do not contain historical data, only data for the specific identified issue which triggered the alert. An alert is a message generated when a predefined event occurs, and these alerts might generate notifications to IT personnel or other automated responses. A log is a record of activities or state changes on a device or in a system; logs contain historical data that can be displayed in a line chart, but the logs themselves don’t contain line charts.
whyWrong: A notification reports one issue and does not usually contain historical data.
An alert is a message generated when a predefined event occurs.
A log is a record of activities, and it does not display charts itself.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Self-Check question 4

stem: What command requests the next record in an SNMP log?
explanation: An NMS uses SNMP Get Request messages to ask an agent for a specific value from its MIB. The Get Next message asks for the next value in the MIB after the last one requested. The NMS can walk through a list of values this way.
whyWrong: A Get Request asks an agent for one specific value.
A trap is a message that an agent sends to the NMS on its own when an event occurs.
A Get Response is the agent's reply to a request.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Review Questions question 1

stem: Which type of disaster recovery site contains all the equipment you would need to get up and running again after a disaster, and yet would require several weeks to implement?
explanation: A cold site has the computers, devices, and connectivity needed to rebuild a network, but they are not configured, updated, or connected. You must install operating systems, restore data, and reconfigure devices before it can work. Even for a small network, this can take weeks.
whyWrong: A warm site has some systems configured and can be ready in hours or days.
Standby site is not one of the standard DR site types.
A hot site is fully configured and can take over almost at once.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Review Questions question 5

stem: Which log type is used to prove who did what and when?
explanation: An audit log records who did what and when in great detail. Its data is thorough enough to prove compliance after the fact. It is often used in forensic investigations.
whyWrong: A traffic log records network traffic, not the actions of each user.
A system log tracks events on a single device.
Syslog is a protocol and format for sending log messages to a collector.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Review Questions question 6

stem: What type of cloud service captures API calls made to change resource configurations?
explanation: Cloud logging services capture activities such as sign-in attempts, configuration changes, and traffic flows. Most cloud platforms use API calls for nearly every change to a resource configuration. A logging service such as AWS CloudTrail records each of these API calls.
whyWrong: An alerting service sends messages when predefined events occur.
A data analysis service analyzes data that has already been collected.
A notification service sends emails, texts, or tickets about an issue.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Review Questions question 8

stem: Which backup type, if performed daily, would offer the lowest RTO and why?
explanation: RTO is the amount of downtime that is acceptable before full functionality is restored. With a daily full backup, you restore one backup set and you are done. Differential and incremental backups need the last full backup plus more backups, so recovery takes longer.
whyWrong: A daily incremental backup has the highest RTO because you must restore every incremental since the last full backup.
An archive backup keeps data for long-term storage and is not the fastest way to restore.
A daily differential backup needs the last full backup plus one differential, which takes longer than one full backup.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Review Questions question 10

stem: One of your coworkers downloaded several very large video files for a special project they’re working on for a new client. When you run your network monitor later this afternoon, what list will your coworker’s computer likely show up on?
explanation: Network monitors identify usage anomalies, such as top talkers and top listeners. Top listeners are hosts that receive an inordinate amount of data. Your coworker downloaded several very large files, so their computer received much more data than usual and would appear on the top listeners list.
whyWrong: Top talkers are hosts that send an inordinate amount of data, not hosts that receive it.
Giants are frames that are larger than the maximum allowed size.
Jabbers are devices that send garbled or oversized frames continuously.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Scenario-Based Questions question 2
note: The book gives no answer; the chapter defines top talkers as senders and top listeners as receivers, so a computer that downloaded large files is a top listener.

stem: When you arrive at work one morning, your inbox is full of messages complaining of a network slowdown. You collect a capture from your network monitor. What documentation can help you determine what has changed?
explanation: A baseline is a record of how the network performs under normal conditions. Comparing the new capture to the baseline shows what has changed. Without a baseline, it is hard to tell whether a reading is unusual.
whyWrong: An SLA defines a provider's service levels, not the normal state of your network.
A DR plan describes how to recover from a disaster.
An audit report reviews compliance and does not show normal network performance.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Scenario-Based Questions question 4

stem: You are configuring a connection from a Windows server to a switch, and you want to make sure the connection doesn’t fail or become overwhelmed by heavy traffic. Which of the following techniques would help you achieve both aims?
explanation: NIC teaming joins two or more network adapters in one server so they work as one connection. If one adapter or link fails, the others keep the connection up. The adapters also share the traffic, so heavy traffic does not overwhelm a single link.
whyWrong: Multipathing gives a server several paths to its storage, not a teamed link to a switch.
CARP lets several routers or firewalls share one IP address for failover.
Clustering joins several servers to act as one, not several adapters in one server.
Trunking carries several VLANs over one link between switches.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 11
note: NIC teaming is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with high-availability approaches.

stem: Suppose you are creating six subnets on a network that leases a group of class C IPv4 addresses to desktop computers, servers, and printers. Because the network rarely needs to connect mobile devices, what DHCP configuration will minimize the number of times a client device must request an updated IP address?
explanation: The lease time sets how long a client may keep its IP address before it must renew it. On a network with mostly stationary devices, a long lease time is a good choice. Clients then request an updated address less often, which reduces DHCP traffic.
whyWrong: A reservation gives one device the same address every time but does not reduce how often clients renew.
A scope is the range of addresses the server can lease, not how long a lease lasts.
An exclusion keeps addresses out of the pool and does not change renewal frequency.
The default gateway option tells clients where to send traffic for other networks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 18

stem: Your organization contracts with a cloud service provider to store some backup data. The company promises 99.999 percent uptime. If it lives up to its claims, what is the maximum number of minutes each year you can expect your data to be unavailable?
explanation: A year has 365 × 24 × 60 = 525,600 minutes. An uptime of 99.999 percent allows 0.001 percent downtime. 525,600 × 0.00001 is about 5.26 minutes of downtime each year.
whyWrong: About 448 minutes of downtime is much more than five nines allows.
About 199 minutes of downtime is much more than five nines allows.
About 52 minutes a year is the downtime for four nines of uptime.
About 14 minutes of downtime is more than five nines allows.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 24
note: Uptime percentages are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with DR metrics.

stem: Your organization is reassessing its WAN connections to determine how much more bandwidth it will need to purchase in the next two years. As a network administrator, which of the following data can you share that will help management make the best decision?
explanation: A baseline is a record of how the network performs under normal conditions, including bandwidth use. When you compare baselines collected over time, you can see how fast usage is growing. This helps management predict how much more bandwidth the WAN connections will need.
whyWrong: A wiring diagram shows how cables connect devices, not how bandwidth use changes.
A logical topology shows how data flows and how the network is addressed, not usage trends.
Syslog messages record events but do not summarize bandwidth trends.
Change management documentation records changes made to the network, not bandwidth use.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 34

stem: Which of the following protocols encapsulates data for transmission over VPNs?
explanation: L2TP (Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol) encapsulates data so that it can travel through a VPN tunnel. It does not encrypt data by itself, so it is usually paired with IPsec. The other options are file transfer, remote desktop, transport, and authentication protocols.
whyWrong: SFTP transfers files securely over SSH and is not a VPN protocol.
RDP gives a remote desktop session and does not create VPN tunnels.
TCP is a transport protocol that provides reliable delivery, not VPN tunneling.
TACACS+ authenticates and authorizes administrators of network devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 39
note: L2TP is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with site-to-site VPN.

stem: You’re installing a network management system and need to install software on various devices. What software must be installed on a managed device, such as a router?
explanation: In SNMP, each managed device runs an agent. The agent collects information about the device and answers requests from the NMS. It can also send traps to the NMS when an event occurs.
whyWrong: A SIEM collects and analyzes security events from many sources.
An OID identifies one managed object in a MIB and is not software.
The NMS is the management software on the central server, not on each device.
Syslog is a protocol for sending log messages to a collector.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 47

stem: You are setting up a new Windows client to connect with your LAN, which relies on DHCP. Which of the following must you do to ensure that the client obtains correct TCP/IP information via DHCP?
options: Make certain the client’s computer name and host name are identical.
Enter the client’s MAC address in the DHCP server’s ARP table.
Nothing; in Windows, the DHCP option is selected by default.
Enter the DHCP server address in the Windows TCP/IP configuration.
Enter a default gateway address in the Windows TCP/IP configuration.
explanation: Windows clients are set to obtain an IP address automatically by default. The client broadcasts a DHCP discover message to find a server. The DHCP server then supplies the IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS server addresses.
whyWrong: The computer name has no effect on whether the client gets an address from DHCP.
DHCP servers do not use an ARP table to assign addresses to clients.
A DHCP client finds the server by broadcasting, so you do not enter the server address.
The DHCP server gives the client its default gateway, so you do not enter it.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 51

stem: You have installed a protocol analyzer on your laptop and connected the laptop to a switch on your network’s backbone. You want to monitor all traffic on a specific VLAN. Which feature must you configure on the switch to make this work?
explanation: A switch sends each frame only to the port of its destination, so a protocol analyzer on another port sees little traffic. Port mirroring copies the traffic from chosen ports or a VLAN to the port where the analyzer is connected. The analyzer can then capture all the traffic on that VLAN.
whyWrong: Trunking carries traffic for several VLANs between switches but does not copy it to your laptop.
A loop is a fault that causes broadcast storms, not a monitoring feature.
Spanning Tree Protocol prevents switching loops.
Caching stores data to answer later requests faster.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 53

stem: About a year ago, you purchased and installed a new router at one of your company’s branch offices, and you have had nothing but problems with the router since. Today you called the vendor for the third time to have them send a technician to repair the router. They estimate the repair will be completed by the end of business tomorrow. In the meantime, you have decided that you would prefer to replace the router the next time it fails. What factor should you carefully investigate when shopping for a replacement, so you won’t face this same scenario with the next router?
explanation: MTBF (mean time between failures) is the average time that passes before a device's next failure is expected. A router with a high MTBF fails less often. Comparing MTBF values helps you choose a more reliable replacement.
whyWrong: MTTR is the average time to repair a failed device, but it does not tell you how often the device fails.
A UPS supplies backup power and has nothing to do with router reliability.
An SLA defines a service provider's obligations, not how reliable the router itself is.
A MIB is the database of objects that SNMP manages.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 57

stem: You are the network administrator for a large university whose network currently contains nearly 10,000 workstations, over 80 routers, 250 switches, and 500 printers. You are researching a proposal to upgrade the routers and switches on your network to primarily use multilayer switches instead. At the same time, you want to improve the management of your network devices. Which of the following protocols will help automate network management across all the new devices?
explanation: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) lets an NMS collect information from and manage many network devices. Each device runs an SNMP agent that answers the NMS and sends traps when events occur. Almost all routers and switches, including multilayer switches, support SNMP.
whyWrong: TFTP transfers files without authentication, such as configuration files or firmware.
SMTP sends email between mail servers.
NTP synchronizes the clocks of network devices.
ICMP carries error and diagnostic messages, such as ping.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 62

stem: To provide redundancy, you need to set up three links from a critical server to two redundant switches, both of which operate on the same subnet. Two connections from the server go to one switch, and the third link connects the other switch to the server. The server is running Windows Server. What feature should you configure on the server to make these redundant links work together for load balancing and failover protection?
explanation: NIC teaming joins several network adapters in a server so that they act as one logical connection. Windows Server supports NIC teaming across adapters connected to different switches on the same subnet. The team balances traffic across the links and keeps working if one link fails.
whyWrong: Port aggregation joins links between the same two devices, but these links go to two different switches.
Flow control manages the rate of data transmission and does not join links.
A server cluster joins several servers, not several network links on one server.
A virtual IP address lets several devices share one address but does not team the links.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 67
note: NIC teaming is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with high-availability approaches.

stem: A file server on your network is running Ubuntu Server. You need to remote into it to make a backup of the server’s configuration settings. Which of the following utilities will give you secure access to the server to make your backup?
explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) is included with all modern Linux distributions, including Ubuntu Server. It gives you an encrypted, authenticated command-line session on the remote server. Telnet does the same job but is not secure.
whyWrong: RDP is a Microsoft remote desktop protocol, mainly used with Windows.
SSL is an encryption protocol, not a remote access utility.
SFTP transfers files securely but does not give you a command session on the server.
Telnet gives remote access but sends everything in plain text.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 71

stem: A regional bank manager asks you to help with an urgent network problem. Because of a sudden and severe network performance decline, the manager worries that the bank’s network might be suffering a DoS attack. Viewing which of the following types of network documentation would probably give you the quickest insight into what’s causing this problem?
options: The main file server’s system log
explanation: A firewall log records the traffic that reaches the network edge, including the source and destination of each connection. During a DoS attack, it quickly shows a flood of traffic from one or many sources. Diagrams and a single server's log do not show this traffic.
whyWrong: A wiring diagram shows physical cable connections and gives no information about traffic.
A logical network diagram shows how the network is addressed, not what traffic is arriving.
A file server's system log shows events on that one server and not the network traffic.
A physical network diagram shows where devices and cables are, not the traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 73

stem: You have created a new web server on a computer running the Linux operating system. Some of the modules aren’t loading correctly, and services are encountering errors. Which of the following applications should you check for information on these errors?
explanation: On Linux systems, syslog collects messages from the kernel, modules, and services. Errors from modules that fail to load and from failing services are recorded there. Event Viewer does the same job on Windows.
whyWrong: Event Viewer is the log viewer on Windows, not Linux.
An IDS detects intrusions and does not record service errors.
A packet sniffer captures network traffic, not service errors.
NetFlow collects traffic flow data, not service errors.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 81

stem: As you’re creating a new website for your organization, you need to add new DNS records for the website and validate your DNS server’s information so other DNS servers will accept the updates. Which standard will meet this requirement?
explanation: DNSSEC (DNS Security Extensions) adds digital signatures to DNS records. Other DNS servers use the signatures to check that the records are valid and come from the right server. DoH and DoT only encrypt the queries in transit.
whyWrong: A CNAME record holds an alternative name for a host and does not validate DNS data.
An NS record identifies the authoritative name servers for a zone.
DoH encrypts DNS queries in HTTPS but does not validate the records themselves.
DoT encrypts DNS queries in TLS but does not validate the records themselves.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 82

stem: Your company is experiencing a growth spurt and is ready to invest in a more sophisticated disaster recovery plan. Currently the backup plan consists of a few spare computers in a storage closet, and data on the servers is duplicated weekly to an off-site backup service. The company owners have committed to acquiring additional servers to duplicate critical servers in their current network, and they want the servers to be configured identically to the servers now in use. The new servers will be stored at an off-site data center and updated every time the on-site servers are updated. What type of disaster recovery site is your company creating?
explanation: A hot site has computers, devices, and connectivity that are configured, updated, and ready to take over. Because the off-site servers are updated every time the on-site servers are, they can take over almost at once. A warm site is updated less often, so it takes longer to restore service.
whyWrong: Ambient site is not a type of disaster recovery site.
A cloud site runs recovery systems in a cloud provider, not on servers the company buys for an off-site data center.
A warm site has duplicate systems that are updated only from time to time, not every time.
Differential is a type of backup, not a type of disaster recovery site.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 89

stem: Which of the following is a secure alternative to Telnet that enables secure sessions to be opened on a remote host?
explanation: SSH is a secure alternative to Telnet that enables secure sessions to be opened on a remote host. SSH uses port 22. It encrypts the whole session, including the password.
whyWrong: RSH is a remote shell that does not encrypt its traffic.
IPsec secures IP traffic between hosts or networks but is not a remote shell.
RDP gives a graphical remote desktop session, mainly on Windows.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security, Cram Quiz 3 question 2

stem: Which of the following types of cables is used to connect a terminal to the console port of a router or switch?
explanation: A rollover cable is a type of null modem cable, usually flat and light blue in color, with the pinouts reversed on either end, to enable a terminal to communicate with a router or switch through the device's dedicated console port. None of the other options are suitable for this purpose. A straight-through cable is the standard network cable used to connect a computer to a switch. A crossover cable is designed to connect two network adapters (in computers or similar devices) to each other directly. A plenum cable is a type of cable intended for use within air spaces that has an outer sheath that does not produce toxic fumes when it burns. A shielded cable is intended to protect signals from electromagnetic interference. A tap is a device used to branch a coaxial cable to two devices.
whyWrong: A straight-through cable connects a computer to a switch, not a terminal to a console port.
A crossover cable connects two network adapters directly to each other.
Plenum describes a fire-rated cable jacket, not a console cable.
Shielded describes protection from electromagnetic interference, not a console cable.
A tap branches a coaxial cable to two devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 5: Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 33

stem: At what point in the installation process should patch panel ports and wall plates be labeled?
options: When the patch panels and wall plates are installed
When a length of cable is cut from the spool
When the cables are attached to the connectors
When the cable runs are tested, immediately after their installation
explanation: Patch panel ports and wall plates should be labeled when the cable runs are attached to them. Labeling them at any earlier time can result in cable runs being connected incorrectly.
whyWrong: Labeling the ports before the cables are attached can leave the labels out of step with the runs that are actually connected.
A cut length of cable is not yet tied to any port, so labeling the ports at that point can produce wrong labels.
The ports are labeled when the runs are attached, which comes before the runs are tested.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 5: Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 75

stem: Ralph is a network administrator for a company with several branch offices, each of which has a Windows domain controller. There have been problems lately with the domain controllers synchronizing their data, and Ralph suspects that the problem is related to the Network Time Protocol (NTP) settings on the servers. Examining the server logs on the various domain controllers, he sees multiple errors saying, “Server NTP service not synchronized.” All of the other server functions are running normally. Which of the following could be the cause of the problem Ralph is experiencing?
options: Unresponsive database service on the servers
Incorrect TCP/IP settings on the servers
Incorrect firewall settings on the servers
explanation: On all of the servers, NTP uses the well-known User Datagram Protocol (UDP) port 123 for its communications with a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) server. If a server's firewall is blocking that port, it cannot synchronize its clock time. If the domain controllers have clocks that are not synchronized, their data synchronization processes can be affected. The problem is not a name resolution failure, an unresponsive database service, or incorrect TCP/IP settings because other server functions are not affected.
whyWrong: Other server functions work normally, so name resolution is not failing.
The errors are about the NTP service, and the other services run normally.
Incorrect TCP/IP settings would affect the other server functions as well.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 5: Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 110

stem: Alice's company is opening a new branch office, and Alice is responsible for building the domain controller for that office. She installs a new Windows server and configures it as a domain controller, and then ships it to the new office site. However, once it arrives and is connected to the home office network, the new domain controller fails to synchronize with the existing ones at the home office. Which of the following could be the cause of the problem?
explanation: If the time on the domain controller at the new office is more than 5 minutes off the time held by domain controller at the home office, then the new domain controller will not synchronize. Duplicate IP addresses or an incorrect default gateway address would prevent the new domain controller from connecting to the home office network. A server hardware failure would manifest as an outage far more serious than a domain controller synchronization issue.
whyWrong: A hardware failure would cause a far more serious outage than a synchronization problem.
Duplicate IP addresses would keep the server from connecting to the home office network at all.
An incorrect default gateway would keep the server from reaching the home office network at all.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 5: Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 111

stem: Alice is troubleshooting a problem that some users are having connecting to an application server on the local network. While testing connectivity using the `ping` tool, she discovers that she can ping the server successfully using its computer name, but pinging the computer's fully qualified domain name (FQDN) fails. Which of the following is MOST LIKELY the source of the problem?
explanation: Only DNS servers perform FQDN resolutions, so that is likely to be the source of the problem. It is possible to ping a device on the local network using its computer name without the use of DNS. Electromagnetic interference (EMI) would inhibit all network communication, and access control lists have no effect on ping tests.
whyWrong: DHCP assigns addresses and does not resolve FQDNs.
Electromagnetic interference would disrupt all traffic, including the ping by computer name.
Access control lists would block the ping in both cases, not just the FQDN.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 5: Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 112

stem: Ralph has begun to receive calls from users reporting that they cannot access the local network or the Internet. Ralph checks their computers and discovers that all of the users with a problem have IP addresses in the 169.254.0.0/16 network, which is not the address used on Ralph's network. Which of the following might be the cause of the problem?
options: The users have tried to modify their IP configuration settings.
There is a rogue DHCP server somewhere on the network.
The IP address leases assigned by the DHCP server have expired.
The users' workstations have been infected by a form of malware.
explanation: The 169.254.0.0/16 network is used by Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA), a standard that provides DHCP clients with an IP address when they cannot contact a DHCP server. Unknown to Ralph, the DHCP server on his network has been down for over a week, and the users' IP address leases have begun to expire. This causes them to revert to APIPA addresses. Multiple users changing their IP addresses would not result in them all using the same network address. A rogue DHCP would not be likely to deploy APIPA addresses to clients. Malware infections that modify IP addresses are rare.
whyWrong: Users changing their own settings would not all end up on the same APIPA network.
A rogue DHCP server hands out its own scope, not APIPA addresses.
Malware that changes IP addresses is rare and would not explain the APIPA addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 5: Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 113

stem: Which of the following tools can administrators use to monitor network bandwidth and traffic patterns?
explanation: A NetFlow analyzer is a tool that can collect network traffic data and analyze how bandwidth is being used and who is using it. A protocol analyzer is also a tool that captures network packets, but for the purpose of analyzing their contents. A bandwidth speed tester measures a network's Internet access speed. An IP scanner lists the IP addresses that are in use on a network. A cable tester measures the properties of the network medium, but not the traffic passing over it.
whyWrong: A protocol analyzer captures packets to examine their contents rather than to chart bandwidth use.
A bandwidth speed tester measures the speed of an Internet connection.
An IP scanner lists the IP addresses in use on a network.
A cable tester checks the cable itself, not the traffic on it.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 5: Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 209

stem: Which of the following is a feature included in some routers that collects and analyzes network traffic data sent or received through a network interface?
explanation: NetFlow is a network traffic monitoring feature first introduced in Cisco routers in 1996. `Netmon`, `netstat`, and `nbtstat` are all operating system utilities, not router features.
whyWrong: `netmon` is an operating system utility for capturing traffic, not a router feature.
`netstat` is an operating system utility that shows connections and statistics.
`nbtstat` is a Windows utility that shows NetBIOS information.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 5: Network Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 232
